verdicts.decision_note: The client requires through-holes providing access to unused ESP32 pins and permits flexible hole placement on the main-board PCB.
The client explicitly expands the breakout to full ESP32-S3 pin access, retains through-hole construction, and defines reuse as a generic base platform.
The client identifies a material uncertainty over whether the 40-position breakout omits GPIOs or only excludes duplicated power and ground connections.
This is the first target-specific implementation claim that all ESP32-S3 module pins are connected to 40 through-hole positions.
The client establishes 40 as the actual module pin count, providing the concrete pin-count acceptance rule for full breakout coverage.
The client resolves the earlier breakout-coverage uncertainty by distinguishing the 40-pin module from a 44-pin development board with duplicated supply pins.
The client accepts an unpopulated through-hole breakout, changing the assembly requirement so physical pin-header connectors need not be supplied.
This exchange concerns connector placement on the integrated board and does not change the main-board ESP32 breakout or extend its scope.

missing_event_candidates.description: The integrated-board exchange establishes connector-placement constraints and accepts flexible placement within those constraints; it should be evaluated under the integrated-board mechanical-layout Requirement.
